Dedicated vs Hosted for cache locality
transcript:
Header: 2025-05-20 10:00 PDT / Duration: 45m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (BlueWave ML), Rajiv Kumar (BlueWave Platform), Nina Park (Product)
Link to artifacts: benchmark sheet (drive): https://drive.google.com/.../bwa-cache-weekly, perf dashboard: https://redwood.in/benchmarks/bwa-cache-05-20

[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, and Samir is here from our infra team. Quick check, is the agenda the same — revisit cache hit numbers, go over the replay anomalies, and plan the Dedicated perf run?
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: Yep that's right, thanks. We got the CSV you sent last week, we dug into some slices.
[00:26] Samir Patel: Great, quick note — the new canonicalization step we pushed Friday normalized about 18% of prompt variants into the prefix cacheable bucket. We saw the global prefix hit rate move from ~21% to ~34 in the last 48 hours.
[00:45] Rajiv Kumar: When you say canonicalization, you mean whitespace and simple token mapping or also argument ordering? We saw some stuff where the same semantic prompt had different param orders.
[00:58] Samir Patel: Both. We started with text normalization (whitespace, punctuation), then moved to deterministic key ordering for JSON-like payloads, and a small phrase-level mapping for common synonyms. Not full semantic canonicalization.
[01:15] Nina Park: That explains some improvement, but our business queries still show low hits for support-chat style prompts.
[01:25] Lena Ortiz: Yeah the long-tail is the problem — a lot of one-off user prompts. Our replay results: out of 12k unique prompt keys over last week only 2.4k hit the KV/prefix cache.
[01:40] Samir Patel: The raw telemetry we sent shows per-model breakdowns: for the short-answer model the prefix hit was 38%, KV global hit 44%, but for the multi-turn assistant model prefix hit was 19% and KV hit 21%.
[01:58] Maya Chen: Are you seeing many near-misses where the cache was >75% similar but not exact? That would indicate we could leverage embedding-based cache lookup.
[02:10] Lena Ortiz: We saw a cluster of prompts that were semantically similar but differed in entity names and timestamps. Embedding approach might help but we're sensitive about storing user content.
[02:25] Rajiv Kumar: Security question — how is the KV cache stored? Is it encrypted, and does it live in our account for Dedicated?
[02:34] Samir Patel: For Hosted POC it's in Redwood's managed store, encrypted at rest with our KMS; logs masked per your PII rules. For Dedicated we can deploy the KV store in your VPC and hook up to your KMS so keys never leave. That was in the security deck we shared.
[02:52] Nina Park: Good. For compliance we need a short doc confirming KMS integration flows.
[03:00] Maya Chen: We'll send the KMS integration note as a follow-up (action item).

--- Auto-summary pasted by recorder: Cache hit rate improved after canonicalization; long-tail prompts remain low. Next steps: telemetry dump, replay with dedup, Dedicated perf run planning.

[03:18] Samir Patel: Back to hit rate specifics — last replay (5/18) we applied a 7-day TTL and got slightly better global KV hits (up ~6 points). But TTL tradeoff: stale cached completions can regress correctness for time-sensitive prompts.
[03:37] Lena Ortiz: We measured accuracy drift on time-sensitive prompts — about a 3% drop for anything older than 2 days. So TTL can't be too long for those classes.
[03:48] Samir Patel: We recommend class-based TTLs: short for time-sensitive queries, longer for static knowledge lookups. Also a validation policy on serve that checks prompt timestamp and invalidates if older than threshold.
[04:04] Rajiv Kumar: That makes sense. How do we identify classes programmatically?
[04:10] Samir Patel: We surfaced a heuristic in the sheet — regex+metadata based tagging (e.g., contains date strings, order IDs) and model-provided intent signal. It gets you >80% coverage for the top classes.
[04:24] Lena Ortiz: On prompt reuse strategy, we tried a simple dedup prior to send and saw 12% fewer unique keys, but that didn't map one-for-one to higher hit rates. We think canonicalization + dedup together is needed.
[04:39] Maya Chen: Right, dedup reduces upstream variance but canonicalization reduces key space. You should see multiplicative benefits when both applied.

[05:00] [05:00] Maya Chen: I want to call out one anomaly — a spike in cache misses for the assistant model between 9-10am on 5/18. Samir, did we see anything on the backend?
[05:12] Samir Patel: Yes, that was an autoscaler event on the Dedicated-like instance where KV index hot-shards were pruned during a GC cycle; miss rate jumped temporarily. We've hardened shard compaction and added backpressure to protect hot keys.
[05:28] Rajiv Kumar: Was that on Dedicated or Hosted?
[05:31] Samir Patel: Hosted POC environment. For Dedicated the topology will be different; we'll keep you posted on test run results.

[05:45] Lena Ortiz: From the replay we did: with canonicalization + dedup we increased prefix hit from 34 to 46 on the sampled 6k queries, KV global hit from 44 to 57. So we're seeing good lift in the sampled data.
[06:02] Maya Chen: Nice! Those numbers are promising. Any change in latency?
[06:08] Rajiv Kumar: Average tail latency improved because more responses came from cache path, but some requests incurred small overhead due to canonicalization step (about +8ms median). Overall p95 improved ~40ms.
[06:22] Samir Patel: The canonicalization cost is negligible relative to generation time. If you're worried we can do canonicalization pre-ingest in your app or at the edge to move CPU cost off the serving path.

[06:35] Nina Park: Can we get sample prompt templates from Redwood for how to rewrite prompts to increase prefix reuse?
[06:41] Maya Chen: Yes, Samir and I prepared a short list — we'll attach it. It includes parameterized templates and a recommended normalized ordering for multi-field prompts.
[06:51] Samir Patel: Also consider turning frequently-changed arguments into explicit variables so the prefix stays stable — e.g., "Summarize the following article: {article_body}" rather than embedding metadata inline.

[07:06] [07:06] Lena Ortiz: One other find — certain user flows produce near-duplicate prompts with small token swaps (typos, punctuation). We could run a lightweight pre-hash that strips punctuation for cache keying only.
[07:18] Samir Patel: We can support tolerant keying: a second-level fuzzy lookup with a cheap edit-distance filter before doing embedding lookups. We'll show the config options.

[07:32] Maya Chen: Regarding Dedicated perf run planning: target week 5/26, 4xA100 (or similar) with pinned model version and warmed KV store. We should define the runbook — synthetic replay of 100k requests, mix traffic 70/30 short-answer vs assistant.
[07:51] Rajiv Kumar: Can you share the exact replay harness and the resource commit required? We need that to get approval.
[07:58] Maya Chen: We'll share the runbook and an itemized resource/pricing estimate — I'll add that to action items.

[08:10] Nina Park: Any concerns about data residency for Dedicated run? We want the KV store in eu-west region (Ireland) for a subset of traffic.
[08:19] Samir Patel: That's fine; Dedicated can be provisioned in eu-west. For Hosted we can't guarantee residency.

[08:30] Lena Ortiz: On the embedding-caching idea — could we do a hybrid: exact match first, then embedding similarity for a small configurable top-K? That might boost hits without large storage.
[08:41] Samir Patel: Exactly. We recommend exact-match -> normalized-match -> embedding-similarity fallback. Embedding fallback should be limited (top-3) and run with a similarity threshold to avoid false positives. Also it should be subject to retention and masking rules.

[09:00] Maya Chen: Quick commercial note — the cost model changes for Dedicated: caching and KV store are in-customer infra (included in commit), while for Hosted we bill based on hit/miss token delta. I'll follow up with a short pricing table.
[09:15] Rajiv Kumar: Helpful. We'll need a line item for expected monthly storage and throughput.

[09:25] Lena Ortiz: One more technical question — do you support per-key TTL and active invalidation API? We need to be able to invalidate by user ID in case of data deletion requests.
[09:36] Samir Patel: Yes; per-key TTL is supported and there's an invalidate-by-prefix API. For Dedicated we can add a privileged invalidate-by-attribute feature in your VPC. We'll document API endpoints.

[09:50] Nina Park: Okay, seems we have solid plan and artifacts. Let's recap next steps.
[09:55] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood sends telemetry dump, canonicalization + prompt templates, Dedicated runbook and pricing. BlueWave runs a 30k replay with dedup and tags low-hit prompts. We schedule Dedicated perf run week of 5/26.
[10:12] Lena Ortiz: I'll add the replay job to our backlog and invite Samir if we hit blockers.
[10:20] Maya Chen: Great. I'll follow up with the docs and the KMS integration note. Thanks everyone.

[10:30] End of call.
